raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview
When all requests are greedy: avoid redundant temperature and seed reads from UVA, reducing the runtime of the `rejection_sample()` chain by 26–66 µs (25–76%), depending on bsz and GPU. Part of sampling latency improvements for the Q4 Roadmap: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61024.

## Claims

- Reduce the combined GPU time of the four-kernel `rejection_sample()` verifier on Blackwell B300 and Hopper H100 for all-greedy batches, including rejected/bonus-token handling. The measurements below cover the kernels together, without attributing gains to individual kernels.
- Reuse existing kernels with `do_not_specialize`, so changing the flag does not create another compiled variant for otherwise identical arguments.

## Performance Benchmarks

Scripts and reproduction: [benchmark harness](https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm-scripts/blob/3c2293886dcca4f199a3a6550b147eee96453fb7/experiments/specdec_sol/bench_greedy_rejection.py), [analysis SQL](https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm-scripts/blob/3c2293886dcca4f199a3a6550b147eee96453fb7/experiments/specdec_sol/analyze_greedy_rejection.sql), [commands and setup](https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm-scripts/blob/3c2293886dcca4f199a3a6550b147eee96453fb7/experiments/specdec_sol/README.md#greedy-verifier-microbenchmark).

The timed region is one complete `rejection_sample()` call, containing these four kernel launches in order:

| Kernel | Change exercised by `all_greedy=True` |
|---|---|
| `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` | Skip the UVA temperature read while computing target argmax statistics. |
| `_rejection_kernel` | Skip UVA temperature and seed reads on the existing greedy verification path. |
| `_resample_kernel` | Skip the UVA temperature read, return early for greedy corrections, and compute the bonus-token argmax without the Gumbel helper's metadata reads. |
| `_insert_resampled_kernel` | Skip the UVA temperature read when finalizing the correction/bonus token. |

<details>
<summary>Benchmark scope, hardware and methodology</summary>

Every latency in the table below measures this four-kernel sequence together. No individual-kernel timings or ablations were collected. Inputs use temperature=0, one-hot drafts (`draft_logits_cache=None`) and `use_block_verification=False`, with synthetic acceptance, FLY and watermarking disabled. The block-verification preparation kernels (`_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` and `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel`) are therefore outside this measurement. CPU detection of `all_greedy`, sampling-parameter/logits processing, draft gathering and downstream output updates are also outside the timed region.

Comparison: **main (`ca8bd4c055`)**, including the masked-vocabulary-block resampling optimization, versus **PR (`13d298f355`)**. Both sampling modules run within the same process on each GPU. B300 SXM6 AC and H100 80GB HBM3, synthetic Gaussian BF16 logits, vocabulary 248,320, production UVA sampling state, CUDA graph replay and cold L2. PyTorch 2.14.0, Triton 3.8.0 and FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 on both GPUs. CUDA/CUPTI versions are 13.2/13.4 on B300 and 13.0/13.0.1 on H100.

Each point is the median of three CUPTI measurement calls, alternating arm order, with 25 ms warmup and 100 ms measurement per call. Ranges below span accepted-prefix cases, rather than confidence intervals. Four target rows use accepted prefixes 0/3, eight target rows use 0/3/7. Target rows include the bonus row. The overview summarizes these dense-logit cases across both GPUs.

The harness uses `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(..., use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True, dry_run_time_ms=25, repeat_time_ms=100)`, with fallback timing disabled. These are combined GPU chain timings, with no end-to-end serving speedup claim.

</details>

| GPU | Requests | Target rows/request | main (ca8bd4c055), µs | PR (13d298f355), µs | Avg delta µs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B300 | 1 | 4 | 43.1–44.7 | 8.8–12.4 | -33.3 |
| B300 | 1 | 8 | 32.3–52.8 | 9.8–16.7 | -28.8 |
| B300 | 32 | 4 | 80.3–109.9 | 24.8–33.6 | -65.9 |
| B300 | 32 | 8 | 80.9–109.9 | 40.4–52.1 | -52.3 |
| B300 | 128 | 4 | 104.7–153.6 | 71.4–94.1 | -46.4 |
| B300 | 128 | 8 | 169.4–218.1 | 125.2–151.7 | -60.7 |
| H100 | 1 | 4 | 34.8–41.0 | 10.1–12.9 | -26.4 |
| H100 | 1 | 8 | 39.8–48.2 | 11.6–16.2 | -31.2 |
| H100 | 32 | 4 | 95.5–96.3 | 35.4–43.8 | -56.3 |
| H100 | 32 | 8 | 110.3–129.5 | 59.2–69.6 | -54.5 |
| H100 | 128 | 4 | 152.1–184.2 | 98.7–120.7 | -58.4 |
| H100 | 128 | 8 | 234.2–282.0 | 180.3–205.9 | -63.1 |

<details>
<summary>Averaging and measurement variability</summary>

Avg delta µs is the arithmetic mean of `PR − main` latencies across the accepted-prefix cases in each row, using each case's median over three measurement calls. Negative values indicate time saved. The overview uses the range of these row averages. Its percentage range likewise averages `100 * (1 - PR / main)` across cases within each row.

Average savings across table rows: **B300 28.8–65.9 µs (30.7–75.8%)**, **H100 26.4–63.1 µs (24.8–69.8%)**. The largest observed within-case spread across the three call medians, `(max-min)/median`, was 39.2% for main and 2.2% for the PR on these dense cases.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Masked-logit benchmark results</summary>

Masked-logit cases use the same matrix with only the top 20 logits retained per row and `skip_masked_vocab_blocks=True` for both implementations, exercising main's masked-block optimization. Filtering happens before timing. These cases save **22.3–77.4 µs (30.8–80.1%) on B300** and **25.6–59.6 µs (21.5–72.8%) on H100**. Their maximum within-case repeat spread is 35.0% for main and 2.5% for the PR.

</details>

## Validation

All **60 input-case comparisons** matched sampled token IDs and counts exactly before timing, covering 360 measurement calls across both GPUs and scenarios.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py
# 103 passed, 17 warnings in 40.88s

uvx pre-commit run --files tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test CI wiring.
```

Sampling-suite configuration: candidate sampling files overlaid on main (`dd4e40142a`).

Real-model equivalence: Qwen3-0.6B, ngram K=8, temperature=0, max_num_seqs=1, prefix caching disabled, eight SPEED-Bench prompts. Toggling only the flag within the same model instance produced identical token IDs for all 512 output tokens per arm, with 354 verification calls per arm. This is an integration equivalence check, not a model quality evaluation. Configuration: candidate sampling files overlaid on main (`0eb619dc`).

## Details

The CPU already owns the temperature metadata, so detecting an all-greedy batch introduces no device synchronization. Masked temperature/seed loads let the existing greedy branches proceed without waiting for UVA reads. The bonus path computes its target argmax directly. Mixed-temperature batches, synthetic acceptance, FLY and watermarking retain their existing path.

`all_greedy` is required, with a Python `bool` annotation at the API and `tl.int1` in the Triton kernels, before the constexpr parameters. Triton rejects the Python `bool` annotation during GPU compilation.

Existing greedy, placeholder, NaN and adaptive-length tests exercise the flag. The existing Buildkite speculative decoding suite selects this module.

Open-work searches found no existing implementation of this MRV2 metadata-load optimization. Legacy sampler shortcuts and temperature-scaling fusion address different work. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
